19.0.s.en: (6) The healing of the blind man on the way to Jericho

19.0.0.en: Christ entered Jericho with the crowds around Him, and a man who was one of the greatest rich men of Jericho heard of Him. He was Zacchaeus, whose name means "pure," and his office was chief of the tax collectors, that is, he paid the taxes for Jericho and all the villages around it, and then collected these Roman taxes arbitrarily and unjustly, gathering manifold amounts. So he was marked by cruelty and injustice along with great wealth.

19.0.1.en: He worked as a chief of the tax collectors, that is, one responsible for a group of tax collectors. The tax collectors collected more than they were entitled to, and so were marked by greed, wealth and cruelty in collecting taxes; how rich, then, how wicked and how far from God must their chief have been.

19.0.2.en: Zacchaeus was amazed by what he had heard of Christ's teachings and miracles, so he longed to see Him. This shows that God has a place in every heart, however far away it may seem.

19.0.3.en: Zacchaeus tried to see Jesus but could not because of the press of the crowd and because he was little of stature, so it became all the harder for him to break through the crowds to see Jesus.

19.0.4.en: When all Zacchaeus's attempts failed, he hit upon an idea, which was to climb a tree beside which Christ would pass. So he hurried and ran, forgetting his position and his wealth, and got ahead of the crowds until he reached a sycamore tree far along the road by which Christ would pass, and he climbed the tree like a boy, giving up his standing in society, and waited for Him to pass. The faith of Zacchaeus appeared clearly in his striving and his seeking to see Christ, and in his humility and his giving up his standing and his attempt to overcome every obstacle, whether the press of the crowd or his short stature.

19.0.5.en: Zacchaeus represents all sinners immersed in evil, yet the voice of God within them calls them, and if they respond with faith, their seeking appears in their search for Christ.

19.0.6.en: The sycamore tree signifies the Cross, and climbing it means bearing sufferings so that a person may see Christ in his life. It also signifies the Church, which the believer holds fast to and so sees Christ; and he must rise from earthly things to heavenly things through detachment and renunciation and love of prayer and contemplation, and then he is able to see God.

19.1.0.en: The crowds did not distract Christ from looking at Zacchaeus, because He seeks those who are far off and every person who is ready for repentance. He even granted him the grace of entering his house and told him to hurry to do so. And He did not only enter but abode and lodged there.

19.1.1.en: If you take a step toward Christ, trust that He sees you, values your striving, helps you and grants you many blessings.

19.2.0.en: Zacchaeus rejoiced greatly, and came down and opened his house to receive Christ in it.

19.3.0.en: Zacchaeus was a symbol of evil in the city, so the crowds were astonished at Christ's entering to him and mingling with him. But Christ was seeking His repentant children, however much bad reputation He bore, in order to save them. This is the feeling of the servant who does not look for people's opinion of him but for God's opinion and the salvation of souls, whatever sufferings and troubles he bears.

19.4.0.en: The faith of Zacchaeus did not stop at trying to see Christ; rather, when He granted him the grace of entering his house, his feelings were moved to repentance, and he expressed it in practice by rejecting the love of money. He promised to distribute half of his goods to the needy, in addition to his repentance for every wrong he had done to any person, and so he applied the Law by restoring fourfold. Let your repentance be practical, by repairing the effects of your sins and walking in the virtue opposite to the sin into which you fell.

19.5.0.en: Christ declared His joy at the salvation of Zacchaeus and his household, for he had become a true son of Abraham by his practical faith, after having been a son in name only because he was a Jew. He also declared the purpose of His Incarnation and the purpose of all His servants, which is to seek the sinners who are far off so that they may repent and be saved from eternal torment, because they are all God's children.

19.6.0.en: As they heard these things: He means His talk concerning Zacchaeus.

19.6.1.en: Immediately appear: quickly, so that He would set up His kingdom in Jerusalem and defeat the Romans, because they thought that the Messiah was an earthly king. While Christ was heading with His disciples to Jerusalem, they were expecting that He would reign as an earthly king in Jerusalem, so Christ seized this opportunity to speak to them about preparing for the true Kingdom of God in eternity.

19.7.0.en: A certain nobleman is Christ, because He is the true God who became incarnate for our salvation. A far country, that is, heaven, to receive again His kingdom and glory.

19.7.1.en: Return: He comes back in His second coming to judge the whole world.

19.8.0.en: Ten servants represent all God's children who believe in Him in the world, because the number ten is the number of perfection.

19.8.1.en: Ten pounds: the pound (mina) is a silver coin equal to 100 drachmas. The number 100 signifies great perfection, so the pound signifies the word of God and His great gifts that He has given us. Occupy till I come: until He returns to them in His second coming on the day of judgment and repays each one according to his works.

19.8.2.en: Occupy: use your abilities that I have given you and strive spiritually to obtain spiritual fruits of worship, virtues and various services.

19.9.0.en: His citizens signify His human children, created in His image and likeness, who reject Him, and signify more particularly the Jews, from whom He was born and who rejected His message.

19.9.1.en: A message (ambassadors): that is, the Jews who persecuted the Apostles and everyone who preaches Christ after His ascension.

19.10.0.en: When he was returned: the second coming of Christ.

19.10.1.en: Having received the kingdom: after receiving the kingdom after His reign in heaven, that is, His being raised up in the Ascension until His second coming. Commanded to be called unto him: He gathers His children to hold them to account on the day of judgment.

19.10.2.en: The money: the abilities He gave to each one, or the word of God which moved them to spiritual striving. That he might know: to declare his righteousness and reward him, or his wickedness and repay him.

19.10.3.en: What he had gained by trading: the extent of his spiritual striving and what he has reached.

19.10.4.en: After the completion of redemption on the Cross and the binding of the devil, and after the time of this life, the day of judgment comes, on which men are held to account for the extent of their faithfulness in their earthly life.

19.11.0.en: The first: each one is judged alone and does not depend on his relationships with others, so that divine justice may be fulfilled.

19.11.1.en: Thy pound: in humility he attributed the pound to God and not to himself, and therefore the spiritual growth he reached is from God, and he did not attribute to himself his labor and spiritual striving.

19.11.2.en: Ten: the perfection of the gain.

19.11.3.en: The one who gained ten pounds signifies God's servants who labored much for Him, in whom the word of God worked with power and perfection, or any Christian who lived in righteousness and godliness, whether in the world or in monastic life.

19.12.0.en: Christ praised the one who gained ten pounds and described him as good and faithful, and rewarded him with authority over ten cities, that is, ten souls, which are the souls he gained by his service, so that they enjoy with him eternal bliss. For the servant has no aim in the possessions of this world; his only aim is the salvation of souls, and so he will be in heaven advanced, like a chief over others and near to God, enjoying His glory; he leads others in praising God and serving Him like the archangels or the rank of the Principalities among the angels.

19.13.0.en: The one who gained five pounds signifies the godly person who by the word of God sanctified his five senses, so God rewarded him with authority over five cities, that is, all his senses, meaning the enjoyment of eternal bliss, and he will be in heaven advanced and a leader of a group of souls in praising God, but in a lower position than the first, because the first one's striving was greater, so he deserved a better place and enjoyed God more.

19.13.1.en: It is to be noticed in this parable that all the servants received one pound, and one was distinguished from another by the measure of his faithfulness in investing the word of God and his abilities.

19.13.2.en: But in the parable of the talents mentioned in (Mt 25:14-30), the abilities from God given to each one differ from the other's, and consequently each one is held to account according to what he received, to teach us to be faithful in what we have received, for we shall be called to account for it, whether much or little. So let us not be proud if we have received much, nor grieve and be small in our own eyes if we have received little, for the lesson lies in faithfulness and not in the abundance or fewness of our abilities.

19.14.0.en: The one who laid up the pound in a napkin is the wicked person who was immersed in the sins of the world and shut the word of God up and prevented it from working in him. Since he separated himself from the word of God, he lost his spiritual sense because of his sloth in striving, so that he did not repent but condemned God as austere, exploitative and unjust, taking up what He laid not down. It is noticed that He mentioned the accounting of only three of his servants and not the ten, for His purpose is to show the kinds of men and the manner of God's reckoning with them.

19.15.0.en: God the Judge answered him with severity and justice, "Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee." Since you knew that I was expecting profit and gain from the pound I gave you, why did you not trade with it, by your faithfulness in carrying out the commandments, or service and seeking the souls that are far off, or the least striving in trying to carry out the commandment? For the bankers used to give them money and then recover it with interest (usury), so the least trading is to put the money with the bankers to gain even a little. That is, this man refused any spiritual striving, immersed in his wicked lusts.

19.16.0.en: Christ commanded that the pound, that is, the word of God, be taken from the wicked servant and given to the one who gained ten pounds, who is the servant who entered the Kingdom with many souls with him, so He gave him in addition glory and extra honor in the Kingdom, which the owner of this pound would have enjoyed.

19.16.1.en: Christ comments that whoever has love and faithfulness in obeying the commandment is given and increased by God in this life and in the age to come, but whoever has no love and obedience to the commandment, everything God granted him is taken from him and he is cast into eternal torment.

19.17.0.en: All the people who by their sins refused that Christ should reign over them will be judged before His glory on the day of judgment, and they will be slain, that is, they will die not once but will suffer death and torment forever in the eternal fire. God has given you a trust like the rest of His children, so be faithful in your time, your abilities and your gifts, and learn from those who strive around you, so that you become zealous like them and experience God's fellowship on earth, and then rejoice all the more in heaven.

19.18.0.en: Christ went on with His disciples, going up to Jerusalem because it is built on a mountain, to accomplish there the salvation of mankind by His death on the Cross.

19.18.1.en: Bethphage: a town near Jerusalem where the priests lived.

19.18.2.en: Bethany: a town near Jerusalem which was a dwelling place of the people. For Christ came for the salvation of all, and everyone shares in your service.

19.18.3.en: The Mount of Olives is located beside Jerusalem, and it points to the Church in which His believing children are planted, full of peace, because the olive tree signifies peace, and they also give oil, which is the work of the Holy Spirit dwelling in them and overflowing from them. So Christ draws near to the Church in which He proclaims His salvation.

19.18.4.en: And He sent two of His disciples to share with Him in the work of salvation, even if it was a small work, for God rejoices in it. Two is a number that represents love, since God makes the two one in the sacrament of marriage.

19.18.5.en: In sum, God rejoices in the love offered by His children.

19.18.6.en: You ought to rise above earthly things to share with Christ in His sufferings, and so rejoice in His salvation.

19.19.0.en: The village over against you: it is Bethphage.

19.19.1.en: A colt tied: on which no one had ever sat, and it signifies mankind far from God, over which God had not reigned but which wandered in its own lusts and did not bear the sufferings of spiritual striving. In the Gospels of Matthew and Mark it is mentioned that it was a colt and an ass, that is, a female donkey, while in the Gospel of Luke the emphasis is on the colt and the mention of the ass that was with it is omitted.

19.19.2.en: Loose him: He asked His two disciples to loose the colt, meaning to loose it from the bonds of the world so that Christ may reign over it.

19.20.0.en: If any man ask you why you loose him: the owners of the colt or their neighbors would object to the colt's being loosed, and they signify those who object to the salvation of God's children when they leave their wicked lusts, but Christ's asking for these souls and His support silences them.

19.20.1.en: The Lord hath need of him: how great is the humility of Christ, who declares His need for the colt; He needs, in His fatherly love, to save mankind.

19.21.0.en: In obedience and trust in God, the two disciples carried out what Christ commanded them, despite the difficulty of this by human logic, since they would be regarded as thieves in the eyes of the colt's owners; but when they obeyed and said the words of Christ, that the Lord had need of him, the owners let the colt go with them. It appears that God had given a sign to the colt's owners so that they would not object to its being taken, and the sign is the word, "The Lord hath need of him." The owners may have been acquaintances and lovers of Christ.

19.21.1.en: If only you would obey the commandment however hard it seems, confident of its blessing and of God's help and truthfulness.

19.22.0.en: When they brought the colt to Jesus, the two disciples took off their garments and put them on it to make it easy for Christ to ride. Taking off garments means submission, for the slave would take off his garment for the one who bought him, declaring his submission to him. Love makes a person give up even his garments, that is, his necessary needs, and he feels that what he gives up is a small offering, and so his whole life is blessed by Christ.

19.23.0.en: The disciples and the crowds vied with one another in spreading their garments on the road to be trodden by the feet of the colt on which Christ rode. On the one hand, the crowds declare their submission and their need that Christ, the great King, reign over them; and on the other, the feet of the colt (which signifies far-off mankind when Christ reigned over it) became a blessing to all people, as happens with God's holy children who have become a light to the world.

19.24.0.en: The mighty works which they had seen: the great miracles Christ did throughout His life, especially strong ones such as raising the dead.

19.24.1.en: The King that cometh in the name of the Lord: the awaited Messiah who comes to reign over the hearts of His children.

19.24.2.en: When He came to the Mount of Olives, which signifies the Church, the cries of His children burst forth in rejoicing, asking for His salvation and His reign over their hearts, because of their faith in His great miracles and the sharing of heaven and the angels who glorify Him.

19.25.0.en: The Pharisees were enraged at the Jews' glorifying Christ as a great king and asked Him to silence them, but He replied to them that if they held their peace, the stones would cry out.

19.25.1.en: The stones cry out: when their eyes were darkened from seeing Him as King over their hearts and they crucified Him, the stones cried out in that the rocks were rent.

19.25.2.en: The stones also signify the Gentiles who worship stones (idols), whose hearts are like stones, far from God; but if the Jews hold their peace and refuse to believe, the Gentiles will believe and glorify God.

19.25.3.en: And this is what happened during the preaching of the Apostles such as St. Paul the Apostle.

19.26.0.en: Christ looked at Jerusalem, and saw by His divine foreknowledge its rebellion against Him and His crucifixion, and the resistance of the priests and Pharisees to the preaching in His name at the hands of the Apostles, and in the end its destruction at the hands of Titus, the Roman commander, in AD 70, and the killing of those in it. He did not want its destruction, and so He grieved over it and expressed His feelings as a man by weeping. This is the second time that Jesus wept: the first was at the tomb of Lazarus, and the third time will come in the garden of Gethsemane, just before His arrest.

19.27.0.en: If thou hadst known: would that you knew.

19.27.1.en: The things which belong unto thy peace: that is, faith in Christ, so that you may receive peace.

19.27.2.en: They are hid from thine eyes: you hid faith from yourself because of your sins.

19.27.3.en: Christ cried out to Jerusalem in sorrow that it did not know the way to its true peace, for it had sought it in pride and material lusts which hid the truth from it, which is that peace is in faith in Christ and submission to Him so that it might receive its salvation.

19.28.0.en: A trench: barriers and walls placed around Jerusalem to obstruct and prevent the Jews' escape from it during the siege.

19.28.1.en: Christ describes what would happen at the destruction of Jerusalem at the hands of the Romans, who would besiege it until it fell into their hands, and would storm it and kill the Jews in it and tear down the temple and all its buildings, because it did not seize the opportunities of repentance that God sent to it, until He finally visited it with His only Son, but it rose up against Him and crucified Him. If only you would not waste the opportunities of God's visiting you with repentance, so that you escape all evils and keep your peace and inward joy.

19.29.s.en: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

19.29.0.en: Although Christ saw all the stubbornness of the Jews and what they would do to Him in His sufferings and crucifixion, He did not cease positive action. When He entered the temple of Solomon on Monday, that is, the day after His entry into Jerusalem (noting that Luke does not care about the order of events as Mark the Evangelist does), He found the priests and temple servants occupied in its courts with trade and material gain, and consequently the whole people occupied with material things, leaving spiritual worship. So He began to drive all these traders out of the temple courts.

19.30.0.en: Christ declared to the priests and to all the people that the house of God is set apart for prayer, but their preoccupation and their exploitation of the temple for trade had made it a den of thieves, since they stole hearts from the love and worship of God into immersion in the love of material things.

19.30.1.en: Beware of using your going to church as an occasion for any other business or human meetings that distract you from the love of God, or you will become a thief in His sight.

19.31.0.en: Christ was not content with driving the wicked out of the temple, but went on proclaiming His satisfying spiritual teachings in the temple every day, in the hope of rescuing some souls from the coming destruction. But sadly the chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people opposed Him instead of helping Him, because they were seeking their positions and their honor, so they did not benefit from His teachings and repent.

19.32.0.en: They could not find what they might do: they found no reason by which to arrest Him or stop His teachings.

19.32.1.en: Despite the malice of their hearts and their words of opposition to Christ, the crowds continued to cling to Him and to His life-giving words, and all their opposition failed.

19.32.2.en: Continue doing good however much the wicked oppose you, for God will support you and give you favor in the eyes of people. Mutual questions: the authority by which Christ works (vv. 1-8):

19.32.3.en: This discourse is also found in (Mt 21:23-27; Mk 11:27-33).

19.32.4.en: 1- And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders, 2- and spake unto him, saying, "Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?" 3- And he answered and said unto them, "I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: 4- The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?" 5- And they reasoned with themselves, saying, "If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not? 6- But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet."

19.32.5.en: 7- And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was. 8- And Jesus said unto them, "Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things."
